context.title: The Bread of Life
context.summary: Jesus feeds five thousand from a boy's five barley loaves and two fish, then walks on the sea. In Capernaum he declares himself the bread of life, and many disciples leave. Peter answers, 'to whom shall we go?'
context.background: It was near Passover (v. 4), the feast recalling the exodus. The crowd links Jesus' miracle to Moses and the manna, and Jesus builds his teaching on that story. Besides the resurrection, this is the only miracle told in all four Gospels.

customs.note: Barley bread was the cheaper bread of ordinary and poor people. The boy's lunch was a humble one.
The bread-like food God provided each morning during Israel's forty years in the wilderness (Exodus 16).

watchFor: The crowd tries to make Jesus king by force (v. 15).
'I am the bread of life' (v. 35), the first of John's great 'I am' sayings.
'Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life' (v. 68).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Philip
people.summary: One of the twelve apostles; a native of Bethsaida, “the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44). He readily responded to the call of Jesus when first addressed to him (43), and forthwith brought Nathanael also to Jesus (45, 46).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: Andrew
people.summary: Manliness, a Greek name; one of the apostles of our Lord. He was of Bethsaida in Galilee (John 1:44), and was the brother of Simon Peter (Matt. 4:18; 10:2).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The foster-father of our Lord (Matt. 1:16; Luke 3:23). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee (Luke 2:4). He is called a “just man.”

people.name: Judas
people.summary: Son of Simon (John 6:71; 13:2, 26), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth (Josh. 15:25). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels.

places.name: sea of Galilee
places.summary: John (6:1; 21:1) calls it the “sea of Tiberias”.

places.name: Capernaum
places.summary: Nahum’s town, a Galilean city frequently mentioned in the history of our Lord. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament. After our Lord’s expulsion from Nazareth (Matt. 4:13-16; Luke 4:16-31), Capernaum became his “own city.”

places.name: Tiberias
places.summary: A city, the modern Tubarich, on the western shore of the Sea of Tiberias. It is said to have been founded by Herod Antipas (A.D. 16), on the site of the ruins of an older city called Rakkath, and to have been thus named by him after the Emperor Tiberius.

events.title: Feeding of Five Thousand
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 14:13 – John 6:14. People: Jesus, Andrew, Philip. Place: Bethsaida.

events.title: Jesus Walks on Water
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 14:22 – John 6:21. People: Jesus, Simon. Place: sea of Galilee.

events.title: Bread of Life Sermon
events.summary: Passage: John 6:22–71. People: Jesus, Simon. Place: Capernaum.
